about.title: West Hollywood Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: West Hollywood draws heavy foot traffic along its retail and nightlife corridors — Santa Monica Boulevard, Sunset Boulevard, Fountain Avenue, and La Cienega Boulevard among them — and with that traffic comes wet floors, cracked sidewalks, uneven pavers, and poorly lit stairwells. When a property owner or business fails to address a known hazard, the people who get hurt are often left sorting out medical bills and lost wages while trying to figure out who's responsible. If you were hurt on someone else's property in West Hollywood, our team can help you understand your options under California premises liability law. These claims often hinge on what the property owner knew and when, so early documentation matters. We work on a contingency basis, so you owe nothing unless your case recovers.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises liability claims usually require showing the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. We can help gather maintenance logs, inspection records, and witness statements to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many West Hollywood businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. We can send a preservation letter quickly so critical video evidence of the hazard and your fall isn't lost.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Bar, Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partly responsible for your fall, you may still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. We can help present the facts in a way that fairly reflects what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in West Hollywood?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government entity owns the property, such as a public sidewalk or building, the deadline is much shorter and involves an early claim-filing step. Talking to an attorney soon after your fall helps make sure no deadline is missed.

items.question: What if I fell in a store or nightlife venue along Santa Monica Boulevard or Sunset Boulevard?
items.answer: Busy commercial corridors like these see a lot of foot traffic, spills, and temporary hazards from deliveries or events. Whether the incident happened inside a restaurant, retail shop, or nightclub, the same notice requirement applies — you'll want to document the hazard and, if possible, ask that any surveillance footage be preserved right away.

items.question: Do I need to pay anything upfront to get help?
items.answer: No. Our service is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your claim results in a recovery. There's no cost to you for reaching out or discussing your case.
